exposure: distance from the meatus urethra to the anus (Gh + Pb)
position of the anterior vaginal wall (Ba)
outcome: anatomic pelvic organ prolapse (aPOP) at 6 weeks postpartum
cohort: Nulliparous pregnant women at a Norwegian university hospital
finding: Larger LHarea, more distensible LAM, longer Gh + Pb, and more caudal Ba at mid-pregnancy were risk factors for aPOP at 6 weeks postpartum, while delivery route and major LAM injuries were not.
